Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer). → [LLM] Known IOC hash match — malicious Steam Workshop wallpaper payloads
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Wallpaper Engine spawning script interpreters or LOLBins · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Dozens of malicious wallpapers found on Steam Workshop: gamers’ accounts at risk
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] DarkKomet 'Synaptics.exe' masquerade dropped by Wallpaper Engine workshop content · [LLM] Steam Workshop wallpaper '._cache_GAME1.exe' launcher execution · [LLM] Trojanised AggregatorHost.dll loaded from non-system path · [LLM] Persistence via Steam Workshop wallpaper content path in Run keys / Scheduled Tasks · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] C2 callback to malicious wallpaper campaign infrastructure · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Steam credential file (loginusers.vdf / ssfn*) accessed by non-Steam process · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
DarkKomet 'Synaptics.exe' masquerade dropped by Wallpaper Engine workshop content AIInstallation High
Hunts the article's named DarkKomet backdoor file 'Synaptics.exe' dropped or executed outside the legitimate Synaptics touchpad driver install path. The legitimate vendor binary lives under Program Files\Synaptics; any other location is suspicious and matches the Steam Workshop wallpaper drop chain described in the article. Rationale: Article body explicitly names 'Synaptics.exe (part of the DarkKomet malware family)' as the dropped backdoor. The Synaptics name is a known legitimate touchpad driver, so anchoring on the binary name outside the vendor path yields a high-fidelity, low-noise alert. IOC bundle of 13 MD5s lets the analyst confirm at the hash level on triage.
ATT&CKT1036.005 T1204.002 T1547.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Synaptics driver installed via OEM image to a non-standard path (Lenovo/Dell reimaging)
  • Synaptics driver portable extracted to a tech bench for troubleshooting
  • Renamed dev binary named Synaptics.exe (extremely rare)
Suppression filter
and InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("setup.exe","msiexec.exe","trustedinstaller.exe") and InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith @"C:\Windows\System32\DriverStore\"
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: pull SHA256/MD5 of the binary and compare against the article's IOC list; check digital signature (legit Synaptics is signed by Synaptics Inc.). Inspect parent process — wallpaper32.exe / wallpaper64.exe / ._cache_GAME1.exe parents are convicting. Step 2 — Contain: isolate the host via Defender Live Response, kill the Synaptics.exe PID, quarantine the binary and any sibling files under the same drop folder. Step 3 — Hunt: search the rest of the fleet for the same MD5, for outbound connections to 120.48.156.17 / 202.144.192.29, and for Steam credential files (loginusers.vdf, ssfn*) accessed by non-Steam processes in the last 30 days.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where FileName =~ "Synaptics.exe"
| where not(FolderPath has @"\Program Files\Synaptics\" or FolderPath has @"\Program Files (x86)\Synaptics\")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256, MD5
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\Synaptics.exe"
| where not(NewProcessName has @"\Program Files\Synaptics\" or NewProcessName has @"\Program Files (x86)\Synaptics\")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Steam Workshop wallpaper '._cache_GAME1.exe' launcher execution AIInstallation High
Hunts the distinctively named secondary launcher '._cache_GAME1.exe' described in the article — it boots the decoy NTRaholic game while simultaneously installing the trojanised AggregatorHost.dll. The '._cache_' filename prefix is unusual for legitimate Windows software and is highly specific to this wallpaper campaign. Rationale: Article verbatim: 'an executable named ._cache_GAME1.exe fires up to boot the actual game, NTRaholic' and 'that ._cache_GAME1.exe module is doing double duty. It simultaneously installs a custom version of a system library called AggregatorHost.dll'. The '._cache_' prefix is article-specific and extremely unusual in benign software.
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1574.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Unity / Unreal asset cache files mis-extracted by user with .exe rename (rare)
  • Custom internal build pipeline staging artefacts with '._cache_' prefix
  • Mac-to-Windows file copy preserving Apple resource-fork '._' prefix on an exe (rare)
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: capture the file's SHA256/MD5 and check against the article IOC list (13 MD5s). Identify the launching wallpaper package — usually under %ProgramFiles(x86)%\Steam\steamapps\workshop\content\431960\<id>\. Step 2 — Contain: kill the process tree (._cache_GAME1.exe, Synaptics.exe, any spawned child), isolate host, quarantine the wallpaper folder. Step 3 — Hunt: pivot on the Steam workshop content ID and check Steam Workshop subscription history; sweep the fleet for the same wallpaper subscription; check DeviceImageLoadEvents for AggregatorHost.dll loaded from non-System32 paths.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName startswith "._cache_" and FileName endswith ".exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, SHA256, MD5
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName matches regex @"(?i)\\\._cache_[^\\]+\.exe$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Wallpaper Engine spawning script interpreters or LOLBins AIExploitation High
Hunts for Wallpaper Engine (wallpaper32.exe / wallpaper64.exe / wallpaper_engine.exe) acting as the parent for cmd.exe, PowerShell, rundll32, regsvr32, mshta, or for unsigned binaries launched from %TEMP%/%APPDATA% — the execution mechanism the article describes as 'foreign code running directly on your computer' via application wallpapers. Rationale: Article body: 'application wallpapers ... essentially allows foreign code to be run directly on your computer ... Cybercriminals took note of this feature and started embedding malware right into these types of wallpapers.' The wallpaper32/64.exe → LOLBin or temp-folder-binary chain is the exact execution model. Steam Workshop content path 431960 is the official Wallpaper Engine Workshop ID.
ATT&CKT1204.001 T1059.001 T1059.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate 'application wallpaper' that embeds a third-party system monitor (e.g. CoreTemp, MSI Afterburner) — typically signed binaries from Program Files
  • Wallpaper Engine auto-updater launching a CEF helper from %APPDATA%
  • Twitch / Discord overlay started by an application wallpaper
  • Game wallpaper that legitimately calls cmd.exe to query system info
Suppression filter
and not (FileName in~ ("cmd.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/c wmic","systeminfo") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "SystemMonitor")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: pull the child SHA256 and check signature; pull the parent's command line which contains the workshop content ID (path '\steamapps\workshop\content\431960\<id>\'). Cross-check that ID against active Steam Workshop reports. Step 2 — Contain: kill the child process tree, quarantine the workshop content folder, unsubscribe the user from the malicious wallpaper via Steam client (or block file write/read on the folder if Steam is critical). Step 3 — Hunt: for every host where this fired, search DeviceFileEvents for files written under the workshop content folder, and DeviceNetworkEvents for connections initiated by wallpaper32/64.exe or its children to 120.48.156.17 / 202.144.192.29.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("wallpaper32.exe","wallpaper64.exe","wallpaper_engine.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
   or FolderPath has_any (@"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\AppData\Roaming\", @"\Users\Public\", @"\steamapps\workshop\content\431960\")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256, MD5
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("wallpaper32.exe","wallpaper64.exe","wallpaper_engine.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
   or NewProcessName has_any (@"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\AppData\Roaming\", @"\Users\Public\", @"\steamapps\workshop\content\431960\")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Trojanised AggregatorHost.dll loaded from non-system path AIInstallation High
Hunts for AggregatorHost.dll loaded from any folder other than %SystemRoot%\System32 / SysWOW64. The article states the malicious '._cache_GAME1.exe' installs a custom AggregatorHost.dll that hijacks the user's Steam session — the legitimate DLL ships only inside the Windows install. Rationale: Article: 'a custom version of a system library called AggregatorHost.dll with a payload inside. This modified library has one main objective: track down the Steam app on the computer and hunt for account credentials.' Legitimate AggregatorHost ships only under %SystemRoot%, so any drop / load from elsewhere is highly fishy and article-specific.
ATT&CKT1574.002 T1036.005 T1056.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Microsoft KIR / SFC repair operation staging the DLL in %TEMP% during a Windows component refresh (rare)
  • IT-deployed sysprep capture extracting Windows components to a build directory
  • Developer testing a custom WAM authentication broker outside System32
Suppression filter
and InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith @"C:\Windows\" and InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("trustedinstaller.exe","tiworker.exe","sfc.exe")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: hash-verify the loaded DLL against the Microsoft signed binary catalog (signtool / get-authenticodesignature). Confirm parent process — _cache_GAME1.exe or other wallpaper-launched binaries are convicting. Step 2 — Contain: isolate host, dump and quarantine the rogue DLL plus any Synaptics.exe sibling, kill the loading process. Force Steam logout for the affected user and rotate the Steam password + revoke active sessions. Step 3 — Hunt: search the fleet for additional AggregatorHost.dll loads from non-system paths over 30d; correlate with DeviceNetworkEvents to 120.48.156.17/ey.php which is the exfil endpoint the rogue DLL uses.
union
  (DeviceImageLoadEvents
   | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
   | where FileName =~ "AggregatorHost.dll"
   | where not(FolderPath has @"\Windows\System32\" or FolderPath has @"\Windows\SysWOW64\" or FolderPath has @"\Windows\WinSxS\")
   | project Timestamp, DeviceName, EventKind = "ImageLoad", FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, MD5, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine),
  (DeviceFileEvents
   | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
   | where FileName =~ "AggregatorHost.dll"
   | where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")

   | project Timestamp, DeviceName, EventKind = strcat("File:",ActionType), FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, MD5, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath = InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where TargetFileName =~ "AggregatorHost.dll"
| where not(TargetFilePath has @"\Windows\System32\" or TargetFilePath has @"\Windows\SysWOW64\" or TargetFilePath has @"\Windows\WinSxS\")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256, TargetFileMD5, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Steam credential file (loginusers.vdf / ssfn*) accessed by non-Steam process AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts for non-Steam processes opening the Steam login persistence files (loginusers.vdf, config.vdf, ssfn*) — the AggregatorHost.dll trojan described in the article reads these to hijack the live Steam session. Anything but steam.exe / steamwebhelper.exe / steamservice.exe touching them is a high-fidelity infostealer signal. Rationale: Article: 'the modified library hijacks the user's live Steam session ... sends all the collected data to a server controlled by the hackers at hxxp://120.48.156[.]17/ey.php'. Steam session hijack requires reading loginusers.vdf / ssfn token files. Excluding the canonical Steam executables yields almost-zero baseline noise.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555 T1005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Steam Cloud backup utility from Valve
  • Steam family sharing config sync tool
  • User-installed Steam library manager (e.g. SLM)
  • AV scanner with non-standard process name reading the file on access
Suppression filter
and InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName !has "Valve"
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: identify the reading process and its SHA256, compare against the article's IOC list. Pivot the process tree to find the parent — wallpaper32/64.exe or ._cache_GAME1.exe are convicting. Step 2 — Contain: isolate host, kill the offending process, force Steam logout via Steam Support (revokes ssfn tokens), reset Steam password, enable Steam Guard. Step 3 — Hunt: across the fleet, look for additional reads of \Steam\config\* by non-Steam parents; pivot on the reading binary's hash to find every host that ran it; sweep DeviceNetworkEvents for callbacks to 120.48.156.17/ey.php.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (FolderPath has @"\Steam\config\" and (FileName in~ ("loginusers.vdf","config.vdf") or FileName startswith "ssfn"))
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("steam.exe","steamservice.exe","steamwebhelper.exe","steamerrorreporter.exe","steamerrorreporter64.exe","steam_bootstrap.exe","explorer.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessSHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetFilePath has @"\Steam\config\"
| where TargetFileName in~ ("loginusers.vdf","config.vdf") or TargetFileName startswith "ssfn"
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("steam.exe","steamservice.exe","steamwebhelper.exe","steamerrorreporter.exe","steamerrorreporter64.exe","steam_bootstrap.exe","explorer.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

C2 callback to malicious wallpaper campaign infrastructure AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts outbound connections from any process to the article's named C2 IPs (120.48.156.17, 202.144.192.29) or to the article's named C2 URL paths (/ey.php, /audit.php, /download2/Themes2.zip). These IOCs are confirmed by Kaspersky's IoC bundle. Rationale: Article verbatim names hxxp://120.48.156[.]17/ey.php as the Steam-session exfil endpoint and the IoC bundle cites http://202.144.192[.]29/audit.php and /download2/Themes2.zip as additional C2/payload URLs. IP-pinned hosting (not a CDN) keeps FPs at near zero.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1041 T1105
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • In-house malware sandbox detonating a sample with internet access
  • Threat-intel team manually browsing the C2 from a research VM
  • Security vendor downloading the sample via proxy with the analyst's user-agent
Suppression filter
and InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("detonator.exe","sandbox.exe","cuckoo.exe")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: identify the initiating process (InitiatingProcessFileName + SHA256). If the SHA matches the IOC list, treat as confirmed compromise. Otherwise spot-check process tree for wallpaper32/64.exe / ._cache_*.exe / Synaptics.exe ancestors. Step 2 — Contain: block 120.48.156.17 and 202.144.192.29 at egress / perimeter / Defender Network Protection; isolate host; force Steam credential rotation and revoke active sessions for the user. Step 3 — Hunt: 30-day sweep of DNS + netflow for the same IPs; pivot the initiating SHA256 to find every host that ran the same loader; check DeviceFileEvents for AggregatorHost.dll drops on those hosts.
union
  (DeviceNetworkEvents
   | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
   | where RemoteIP in ("120.48.156.17","202.144.192.29")
      or RemoteUrl has_any ("/ey.php","/audit.php","/download2/Themes2.zip")
   | project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessSHA256, InitiatingProcessAccountName),
  (DeviceEvents
   | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
   | where ActionType in ("DnsQueryResponse","ConnectionSuccess")
   | where RemoteIP in ("120.48.156.17","202.144.192.29")
      or RemoteUrl has_any ("/ey.php","/audit.php","/download2/Themes2.zip")
   | project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort=tostring(RemotePort), RemoteUrl, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessSHA256=InitiatingProcessSHA256, InitiatingProcessAccountName)
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
  (CommonSecurityLog
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
   | where DestinationIP in ("120.48.156.17","202.144.192.29")
      or RequestURL has_any ("/ey.php","/audit.php","/download2/Themes2.zip")
   | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, RequestURL, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, SourceUserName),
  (ImNetworkSession
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
   | where DstIpAddr in ("120.48.156.17","202.144.192.29") or Url has_any ("/ey.php","/audit.php","/download2/Themes2.zip")
   | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkApplicationProtocol),
  (DnsEvents
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
   | where Name in ("120.48.156.17","202.144.192.29")
   | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Known IOC hash match — malicious Steam Workshop wallpaper payloads AIWeaponization High
Direct-match sweep for the 13 MD5s published in Kaspersky's IoC bundle across process creation, file write, and image load telemetry. Use as a one-shot retrohunt and as a low-noise ongoing alert. Rationale: Article publishes 13 MD5s in the IoC section — a direct hash sweep is the cheapest, highest-fidelity backstop to behavioural detections. Hash match alone is convicting; correlate with the C2/file/registry detections for full kill-chain context.
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • VirusTotal / Hybrid Analysis researcher manually executing one of the samples on a lab machine
  • AV vendor reverse engineering team sharing samples through the corporate file share
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: confirm hash on disk, capture the binary, identify drop source (Steam Workshop content folder is the convicting parent path). Step 2 — Contain: isolate host, block all 13 MD5s in Defender ASR file-block / file-quarantine policy, push the hash list to firewall sandbox/proxy AV. Step 3 — Hunt: retrohunt 90 days for the same hashes; pivot on each host's Steam Workshop subscription list for the malicious wallpaper content ID; cross-reference with the C2 IP detection results.
let IOCs = dynamic(["95856f2ce428c728d9781d3296558068","af080780cca2acd1d082ce01e7cc346a","c133c3dd9f7d6934598025047df41abf","d1693bbff456ae8fa3360446706df6da","8c2cc585ad8a13a72a704c0fda0c9854","b9fa763a53da3eea742d0f3c845a8c09","ded08ae5df7f1b12e5fdb767dbbed0b1","20965254e29104986e11939decd39549","18dedc0009f0927cba6425c84cce9883","0f4f01c6d495abb37403072dd017ce8d","5620f01284329f561b1839a36be55355","fe1f6485013cd5e6d5cf718049b0b8d6","74414ed4b63aadec039b603c32762b80"]);
union
  (DeviceProcessEvents | where Timestamp > ago(30d) | where MD5 in (IOCs) | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, Source="DeviceProcessEvents", FileName, FolderPath, MD5, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName),
  (DeviceFileEvents    | where Timestamp > ago(30d) | where MD5 in (IOCs) | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, Source="DeviceFileEvents", FileName, FolderPath, MD5, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName),
  (DeviceImageLoadEvents | where Timestamp > ago(30d) | where MD5 in (IOCs) | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, Source="DeviceImageLoadEvents", FileName, FolderPath, MD5, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName)
| order by Timestamp desc
let IOCs = dynamic(["95856f2ce428c728d9781d3296558068","af080780cca2acd1d082ce01e7cc346a","c133c3dd9f7d6934598025047df41abf","d1693bbff456ae8fa3360446706df6da","8c2cc585ad8a13a72a704c0fda0c9854","b9fa763a53da3eea742d0f3c845a8c09","ded08ae5df7f1b12e5fdb767dbbed0b1","20965254e29104986e11939decd39549","18dedc0009f0927cba6425c84cce9883","0f4f01c6d495abb37403072dd017ce8d","5620f01284329f561b1839a36be55355","fe1f6485013cd5e6d5cf718049b0b8d6","74414ed4b63aadec039b603c32762b80"]);
union isfuzzy=true
  (SecurityEvent | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where EventID == 4688 | where FileHash in (IOCs) or tolower(FileHash) in (IOCs) | project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, FileHash),
  (ImFileEvent  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where TargetFileMD5 in (IOCs) | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileMD5, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine)

Persistence via Steam Workshop wallpaper content path in Run keys / Scheduled Tasks AIInstallation Medium
Hunts for autorun keys (HKCU/HKLM Run, RunOnce, Image File Execution Options, scheduled tasks) whose target executable lives under the Wallpaper Engine Steam Workshop content folder (Steam app 431960) or whose target is the article's named binaries (Synaptics.exe, AggregatorHost.dll, ._cache_*.exe). Legitimate wallpapers do not need autorun keys outside of Wallpaper Engine itself. Rationale: Article: 'leave the victim's system infected with backdoors or crypto miners' — backdoors / miners need to survive reboot. Persistence pointing at the Steam Workshop content folder for app 431960 (Wallpaper Engine's Workshop ID) is article-specific. Also catches Run-key persistence pointing at the article's named binaries.
ATT&CKT1547.001 T1053.005 T1574.011
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Wallpaper Engine's own auto-start key (points at Program Files\Wallpaper Engine\, not workshop content — already filtered by the value-data match)
  • User installing a legitimate Workshop wallpaper that ships its own helper EXE and pins a Run key (unusual but possible)
  • Antivirus quarantine restore creating Run key pointing at restored Synaptics.exe in a non-vendor path
Suppression filter
and not (RegistryValueData has @"\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\wallpaper_engine\" and InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "wallpaper64.exe")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: read the offending Run/Scheduled-Task value; confirm the target binary's SHA256 against the IOC list. Identify the writing process (InitiatingProcessFileName) — wallpaper32/64.exe or ._cache_*.exe are convicting. Step 2 — Contain: delete the Run key / scheduled task, kill any running instance of the target binary, quarantine the target file, isolate the host. Step 3 — Hunt: across fleet, look for any other Run/RunOnce/IFEO/SchedTask pointing at \steamapps\workshop\content\431960\; sweep DeviceFileEvents for the SHA256 of the persisted binary; verify whether the user has Steam Workshop subscriptions to identified malicious content IDs.
union
  (DeviceRegistryEvents
   | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
   | where ActionType in ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryKeyCreated")
   | where RegistryKey has_any (@"\CurrentVersion\Run", @"\CurrentVersion\RunOnce", @"\Image File Execution Options\", @"\Wow6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run")
   | where RegistryValueData has_any (@"\steamapps\workshop\content\431960\", "Synaptics.exe", "AggregatorHost.dll", "._cache_")
   | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath),
  (DeviceEvents
   | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
   | where ActionType in ("ScheduledTaskCreated","ScheduledTaskUpdated")
   | where AdditionalFields has_any (@"\steamapps\workshop\content\431960\", "Synaptics.exe", "AggregatorHost.dll", "._cache_")
   | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, AdditionalFields)
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
  (ImRegistryEvent
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
   | where RegistryKey has_any (@"\CurrentVersion\Run", @"\CurrentVersion\RunOnce", @"\Image File Execution Options\")
   | where RegistryValueData has_any (@"\steamapps\workshop\content\431960\", "Synaptics.exe", "AggregatorHost.dll", "._cache_")
   | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, RegistryKey, RegistryValue, RegistryValueData, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine),
  (SecurityEvent
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
   | where EventID in (4698,4702)
   | where EventData has_any (@"\steamapps\workshop\content\431960\", "Synaptics.exe", "AggregatorHost.dll", "._cache_")
   | project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, EventID, Activity, EventData)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Persistence Pointing at Wallpaper Engine Workshop Content or Campaign Binaries
id: 5d2f8c14-3b9a-4e02-9d61-6e3a7b1c4d09
description: Detects Registry Run/RunOnce/IFEO values or scheduled tasks whose target points into the Wallpaper Engine Steam Workshop content folder (Steam app 431960) or to the named campaign binaries (Synaptics.exe, AggregatorHost.dll, ._cache_*.exe).
references:
  - https://securelist.com/dozens-of-malicious-wallpapers-found-on-steam-workshop/120186/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/16
tags:
  - attack.t1547.001
  - attack.t1053.005
  - attack.persistence
logsource:
  category: registry_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_key:
    TargetObject|contains:
      - '\CurrentVersion\Run'
      - '\CurrentVersion\RunOnce'
      - '\Image File Execution Options\'
  selection_value:
    Details|contains:
      - '\steamapps\workshop\content\431960\'
      - 'Synaptics.exe'
      - 'AggregatorHost.dll'
      - '._cache_'
  condition: selection_key and selection_value
falsepositives:
  - Wallpaper Engine itself writing its own startup key — typically points at \Wallpaper Engine\wallpaper64.exe in Program Files, not the workshop content folder
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:13 (@TargetObject:(*\\CurrentVersion\\Run\\* OR *\\CurrentVersion\\RunOnce\\* OR *\\Image?File?Execution?Options\\* OR *\\currentversion\\run\\*)) (@Details:(*\\steamapps\\workshop\\content\\431960\\* OR *Synaptics.exe* OR *synaptics.exe* OR *AggregatorHost.dll* OR *aggregatorhost.dll* OR *._cache_*))
#event_simpleName=AsepValueUpdate (RegObjectName=/\\CurrentVersion\\(Run|RunOnce)/i OR RegObjectName=/\\Image File Execution Options\\/i) (RegStringValue=/\\steamapps\\workshop\\content\\431960\\/i OR RegStringValue=/Synaptics\.exe/i OR RegStringValue=/AggregatorHost\.dll/i OR RegStringValue=/\._cache_/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, RegObjectName, RegValueName, RegStringValue, ContextImageFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime FROM datamodel=Endpoint.Registry WHERE (Registry.registry_path LIKE "%\\CurrentVersion\\Run%" OR Registry.registry_path LIKE "%\\CurrentVersion\\RunOnce%" OR Registry.registry_path LIKE "%\\Image File Execution Options\\%") AND (Registry.registry_value_data LIKE "%\\steamapps\\workshop\\content\\431960\\%" OR Registry.registry_value_data LIKE "%Synaptics.exe%" OR Registry.registry_value_data LIKE "%AggregatorHost.dll%" OR Registry.registry_value_data LIKE "%._cache_%.exe%") BY Registry.dest Registry.user Registry.registry_path Registry.registry_value_name Registry.registry_value_data Registry.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime FROM datamodel=Endpoint.Registry WHERE (Registry.registry_path LIKE "%\\CurrentVersion\\Run%" OR Registry.registry_path LIKE "%\\CurrentVersion\\RunOnce%" OR Registry.registry_path LIKE "%\\Image File Execution Options\\%") AND (Registry.registry_value_data LIKE "%\\steamapps\\workshop\\content\\431960\\%" OR Registry.registry_value_data LIKE "%Synaptics.exe%" OR Registry.registry_value_data LIKE "%AggregatorHost.dll%" OR Registry.registry_value_data LIKE "%._cache_%.exe%") BY Registry.dest Registry.user Registry.registry_path Registry.registry_value_name Registry.registry_value_data Registry.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("202.144.192.29", "120.48.156.17") or RemoteUrl has_any ("brightly.to")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic(["202.144.192.29", "120.48.156.17"]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["brightly.to"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__IP_LIST__` / `__DOMAIN_LIST__` placeholders with
    article-specific destinations. For dynamic IOC management, use a
    watchlist or external feed.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/tactics/TA0011/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.command-and-control
logsource:
    category: network_connection
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_ip:
        DestinationIp:
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    selection_domain:
        DestinationHostname:
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    condition: selection_ip or selection_domain
falsepositives:
    - None on a true-positive IOC match
level: critical
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.dest IN ("202.144.192.29", "120.48.156.17")
    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("brightly.to")
        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("brightly.to")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.dest IN ("202.144.192.29", "120.48.156.17")
    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("brightly.to")
        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("brightly.to")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.

Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High

Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents

union
    ( DeviceFileEvents

        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("95856f2ce428c728d9781d3296558068", "af080780cca2acd1d082ce01e7cc346a", "c133c3dd9f7d6934598025047df41abf", "d1693bbff456ae8fa3360446706df6da", "8c2cc585ad8a13a72a704c0fda0c9854", "b9fa763a53da3eea742d0f3c845a8c09", "ded08ae5df7f1b12e5fdb767dbbed0b1", "20965254e29104986e11939decd39549", "18dedc0009f0927cba6425c84cce9883", "0f4f01c6d495abb37403072dd017ce8d", "5620f01284329f561b1839a36be55355", "fe1f6485013cd5e6d5cf718049b0b8d6", "74414ed4b63aadec039b603c32762b80") or SHA1 in~ ("95856f2ce428c728d9781d3296558068", "af080780cca2acd1d082ce01e7cc346a", "c133c3dd9f7d6934598025047df41abf", "d1693bbff456ae8fa3360446706df6da", "8c2cc585ad8a13a72a704c0fda0c9854", "b9fa763a53da3eea742d0f3c845a8c09", "ded08ae5df7f1b12e5fdb767dbbed0b1", "20965254e29104986e11939decd39549", "18dedc0009f0927cba6425c84cce9883", "0f4f01c6d495abb37403072dd017ce8d", "5620f01284329f561b1839a36be55355", "fe1f6485013cd5e6d5cf718049b0b8d6", "74414ed4b63aadec039b603c32762b80") or MD5 in~ ("95856f2ce428c728d9781d3296558068", "af080780cca2acd1d082ce01e7cc346a", "c133c3dd9f7d6934598025047df41abf", "d1693bbff456ae8fa3360446706df6da", "8c2cc585ad8a13a72a704c0fda0c9854", "b9fa763a53da3eea742d0f3c845a8c09", "ded08ae5df7f1b12e5fdb767dbbed0b1", "20965254e29104986e11939decd39549", "18dedc0009f0927cba6425c84cce9883", "0f4f01c6d495abb37403072dd017ce8d", "5620f01284329f561b1839a36be55355", "fe1f6485013cd5e6d5cf718049b0b8d6", "74414ed4b63aadec039b603c32762b80")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("95856f2ce428c728d9781d3296558068", "af080780cca2acd1d082ce01e7cc346a", "c133c3dd9f7d6934598025047df41abf", "d1693bbff456ae8fa3360446706df6da", "8c2cc585ad8a13a72a704c0fda0c9854", "b9fa763a53da3eea742d0f3c845a8c09", "ded08ae5df7f1b12e5fdb767dbbed0b1", "20965254e29104986e11939decd39549", "18dedc0009f0927cba6425c84cce9883", "0f4f01c6d495abb37403072dd017ce8d", "5620f01284329f561b1839a36be55355", "fe1f6485013cd5e6d5cf718049b0b8d6", "74414ed4b63aadec039b603c32762b80") or SHA1 in~ ("95856f2ce428c728d9781d3296558068", "af080780cca2acd1d082ce01e7cc346a", "c133c3dd9f7d6934598025047df41abf", "d1693bbff456ae8fa3360446706df6da", "8c2cc585ad8a13a72a704c0fda0c9854", "b9fa763a53da3eea742d0f3c845a8c09", "ded08ae5df7f1b12e5fdb767dbbed0b1", "20965254e29104986e11939decd39549", "18dedc0009f0927cba6425c84cce9883", "0f4f01c6d495abb37403072dd017ce8d", "5620f01284329f561b1839a36be55355", "fe1f6485013cd5e6d5cf718049b0b8d6", "74414ed4b63aadec039b603c32762b80") or MD5 in~ ("95856f2ce428c728d9781d3296558068", "af080780cca2acd1d082ce01e7cc346a", "c133c3dd9f7d6934598025047df41abf", "d1693bbff456ae8fa3360446706df6da", "8c2cc585ad8a13a72a704c0fda0c9854", "b9fa763a53da3eea742d0f3c845a8c09", "ded08ae5df7f1b12e5fdb767dbbed0b1", "20965254e29104986e11939decd39549", "18dedc0009f0927cba6425c84cce9883", "0f4f01c6d495abb37403072dd017ce8d", "5620f01284329f561b1839a36be55355", "fe1f6485013cd5e6d5cf718049b0b8d6", "74414ed4b63aadec039b603c32762b80")

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["95856f2ce428c728d9781d3296558068", "af080780cca2acd1d082ce01e7cc346a", "c133c3dd9f7d6934598025047df41abf", "d1693bbff456ae8fa3360446706df6da", "8c2cc585ad8a13a72a704c0fda0c9854", "b9fa763a53da3eea742d0f3c845a8c09", "ded08ae5df7f1b12e5fdb767dbbed0b1", "20965254e29104986e11939decd39549", "18dedc0009f0927cba6425c84cce9883", "0f4f01c6d495abb37403072dd017ce8d", "5620f01284329f561b1839a36be55355", "fe1f6485013cd5e6d5cf718049b0b8d6", "74414ed4b63aadec039b603c32762b80"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] WIN_DRV kernel driver service installed from non-system path · [LLM] SprySOCKS WIN_DRV / WIN_PLUS binary hash hit on Windows endpoint · [LLM] Boot Manager / BCD tampering indicative of CVE-2023-24932 BlackLotus-style UEFI bootkit · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] SprySOCKS Windows C2 egress to FishMonger infrastructure 207.148.78.36 / 207.148.75.122 · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
SprySOCKS Windows C2 egress to FishMonger infrastructure 207.148.78.36 / 207.148.75.122 AICommand & Control Medium
Detects outbound TCP/UDP connections from Windows endpoints to the hardcoded C&C IPs used by SprySOCKS WIN_DRV/WIN_PLUS variants. Article-specific because these are operator-controlled Vultr IPs baked into the backdoor's compiled configuration, not crawled telemetry. Rationale: Direct match on the two hardcoded C2 IPs (207.148.78.36 / 207.148.75.122) ESET published. These are operator-controlled Vultr addresses baked into the WIN_DRV/WIN_PLUS samples — no legitimate enterprise traffic should reach them. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1033/ • https://www.trendmicro.com/en_us/research/23/i/earth-lusca-employs-new-linux-backdoor.html
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1095
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security researcher / threat-intel team intentionally connecting to the IPs from a sandbox VM
  • Outbound NAT IP collisions if a corporate proxy briefly shared a /24 with Vultr
  • Vulnerability scanners targeting the IPs from a known-scanner host
  • Network device sending NetFlow/syslog through a Vultr-hosted aggregator
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("207.148.78.36","207.148.75.122")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull DeviceNetworkEvents around the hit and identify the InitiatingProcessFileName + folder path; check whether the binary is signed and whether parent is a service host or anomalous LOLBin. 2) Contain: isolate the host via Defender MDE Machine Isolation, block both C2 IPs at the perimeter, capture memory and the binary for hash submission. 3) Hunt: pivot on the binary SHA256 across DeviceProcessEvents and DeviceFileEvents for the last 90 days; query DeviceRegistryEvents for new Services keys created by the same process; review DeviceLogonEvents for the user account around the C2 callback.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in ("207.148.78.36", "207.148.75.122")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Protocol, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
let cc_ips = dynamic(["207.148.78.36", "207.148.75.122"]);
(union isfuzzy=true
    (CommonSecurityLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where DestinationIP in (cc_ips)
        | project TimeGenerated, SrcHost = SourceHostName, SrcIP = SourceIP, DstIP = DestinationIP, DstPort = DestinationPort, Proto = Protocol, App = DeviceProduct),
    (ImNetworkSession
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where DstIpAddr in (cc_ips)
        | project TimeGenerated, SrcHost = SrcHostname, SrcIP = SrcIpAddr, DstIP = DstIpAddr, DstPort = DstPortNumber, Proto = NetworkProtocol, App = EventProduct)
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

WIN_DRV kernel driver service installed from non-system path AIInstallation High
SprySOCKS WIN_DRV loads a kernel driver to hide processes, files, registry keys and network connections. Detects service installation events (EID 7045 / 4697) where service type indicates a kernel-mode driver and the image path is outside the canonical Windows driver directories — the article calls out kernel-driver-based rootkit behaviour as the WIN_DRV signature. Rationale: Article specifies WIN_DRV uses kernel drivers to hide network connections, processes, files and registry keys. ServiceType=kernel + non-system path is the install signature. Excluding the four legitimate driver paths keeps FPs to genuinely rare WHQL-bypass or rootkit installs. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1543/003/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1014/
ATT&CKT1543.003 T1014 T1068
Data sourcesEndpoint.Services
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • VPN client installers (Cisco AnyConnect, GlobalProtect) dropping drivers under Program Files
  • Endpoint security tools (CrowdStrike, SentinelOne) installing kernel sensors
  • Virtualisation tooling (VMware Tools, VirtualBox guest additions) installing drivers from vendor folders
  • Hardware vendor drivers (Dell, HP) installed via OEM updater into Program Files\<Vendor>
Suppression filter
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$" | where ServiceFileName !has_any ("\\Program Files\\Cisco\\", "\\Program Files\\CrowdStrike\\", "\\Program Files\\VMware\\", "\\Program Files\\SentinelOne\\", "\\Program Files\\Palo Alto Networks\\")
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture the .sys file, verify Authenticode signer and WHQL status; pull EID 6 (Sysmon driver load) on the same host to confirm load succeeded. 2) Contain: if signer is untrusted or unsigned, isolate the host and submit the driver hash to threat intel; disable the service via Defender Live Response (sc.exe stop / delete). 3) Hunt: search DeviceNetworkEvents from the host for callbacks to 207.148.78.36 / 207.148.75.122; query DeviceFileEvents for the .sys hash across the fleet; check DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities for CVE-2023-24932 exposure on the same hosts.
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("DriverLoad", "ServiceInstalled")
| where FolderPath !startswith @"C:\Windows\System32\drivers\"
    and FolderPath !startswith @"C:\Windows\SysWOW64\drivers\"
    and FolderPath !startswith @"C:\Windows\System32\DriverStore\"
| where FileName endswith ".sys"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4697
| where ServiceType has "kernel"
| where ServiceFileName !startswith @"C:\Windows\System32\drivers\"
    and ServiceFileName !startswith @"\??\C:\Windows\System32\drivers\"
    and ServiceFileName !startswith @"C:\Windows\SysWOW64\drivers\"
    and ServiceFileName !startswith @"C:\Windows\System32\DriverStore\"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ServiceName, ServiceFileName, ServiceType, ServiceStartType, ServiceAccount
| order by TimeGenerated desc

SprySOCKS WIN_DRV / WIN_PLUS binary hash hit on Windows endpoint AIInstallation Medium
Detects execution or write of any of the 11 SHA1 hashes ESET attributes to SprySOCKS WIN_DRV and WIN_PLUS Windows variants. High-fidelity binary-match detection that flags both already-installed implants and fresh drops. Rationale: All 11 SHA1 hashes are pulled directly from the ESET article as confirmed SprySOCKS Windows variant samples. Hash equality is the highest-confidence detection shape — zero ambiguity on intent. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1033/
ATT&CKT1059 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Sandbox / malware analyst VM detonating the sample under controlled conditions
  • Threat-intel team intentionally pulling samples for YARA validation
  • Backup/forensics tools (FTK Imager, X-Ways) reading the binary while imaging an infected host's disk
  • Defender/AV file-scan event re-touching a quarantined sample
Suppression filter
| where not (DeviceName has_any ("SANDBOX", "MALWARE", "FORENSIC", "-IR-"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm hash via Defender DeviceFileEvents — record DeviceName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, AccountName. Differentiate execution (DeviceProcessEvents) vs dormant on-disk (DeviceFileEvents only). 2) Contain: isolate the host, capture memory + the binary, block the SHA1/SHA256 fleet-wide via Defender custom indicator. 3) Hunt: pivot on Vultr C2 IPs 207.148.78.36 / 207.148.75.122 across DeviceNetworkEvents for the last 90d; review DeviceLogonEvents on the infected host for the user account and check IdentityLogonEvents for lateral pivots; query DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities for CVE-2023-24932 exposure on the same host given possible UEFI bootkit chaining.
let sprysocks_sha1 = dynamic([
    "955BFC3DCC867256F9F46A606DEB0779FA3416D8",
    "44DC4A08C5EB0972C8E18B0E01284E06F09006BB",
    "AB87B29B6F79487C75CA08D102E79001E536F083",
    "6490B8E4AADE25A3EE2DA9A47F312DB2122470BC",
    "E7484C24B88A1A2407A8F09D734F9A993670285B",
    "621D1952839BE4B0A1B0E66E87BCE5062CA368ED",
    "2457EED2AB28E37741F10914EF929DAD2C8079D4",
    "D2C706B1EAF662BF0CE124B5032F73ED84BDA24A",
    "5F3B87CEF56683D9A9E19186E0FD0D8019B559C4",
    "C793CA31E3F6628B5C8986146953BF66232E9A30",
    "037DB2445F3D72388CB2CF8510563148E5A184BE"]);
union isfuzzy=true
    (DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(90d)
        | where SHA1 in (sprysocks_sha1)
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, Event = "ProcessExecution", FileName, FolderPath, SHA1, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine),

| order by Timestamp desc

Boot Manager / BCD tampering indicative of CVE-2023-24932 BlackLotus-style UEFI bootkit AIInstallation Medium
ESET reports limited indications SprySOCKS deployment may chain a UEFI bootkit possibly exploiting CVE-2023-24932 (BlackLotus's Secure Boot bypass). Detects writes to the EFI System Partition boot manager and BCD modifications using bcdedit that are the on-disk signature of bootkit installation. Rationale: ESET explicitly notes possible CVE-2023-24932 (BlackLotus Secure Boot bypass) chaining. The canonical BlackLotus install signature is replacing bootmgfw.efi / bootx64.efi on the EFI system partition, or bcdedit modifying the bootmgr description / path. Excluding TrustedInstaller / MoUsoCoreWorker / setup.exe filters legitimate Windows Update boot manager refresh. Cross-checked against: • https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2023-24932 • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/bootkitty-analyzing-first-uefi-bootkit-linux/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1542/003/
ATT&CKT1542.003 T1547.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Windows Update KB5025885 / cumulative servicing pass refreshing boot manager outside TrustedInstaller wrapping
  • Dual-boot Linux installation writing to \EFI\Boot\bootx64.efi from a live USB
  • Disk-imaging restore (Veeam / Acronis bare-metal) rewriting EFI partition
  • Manual recovery — admin running bcdedit /set or bootrec /fixboot during repair
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("TrustedInstaller.exe","MoUsoCoreWorker.exe","wuauclt.exe","setup.exe","bcdboot.exe","BootRec.exe") and InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("services.exe","wininit.exe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull DeviceFileEvents to identify writing process + parent chain; collect the new .efi binary hash and verify Authenticode against Microsoft signer. Cross-check OS build vs KB5025885 / KB5036896 install state to rule out a real Windows Update servicing pass. 2) Contain: if signer is non-Microsoft or process chain is suspicious, image the disk before reboot (bootkit may persist across OS reinstall), isolate the host, escalate to IR for offline EFI analysis. 3) Hunt: query DeviceNetworkEvents for SprySOCKS C2 (207.148.78.36 / 207.148.75.122) from the same host; check DeviceProcessEvents for any of the 11 SprySOCKS SHA1s; pivot DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities for CVE-2023-24932 unpatched hosts across the fleet.
union isfuzzy=true
    (DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
        | where FolderPath has_any (@"\EFI\Microsoft\Boot\", @"\EFI\Boot\")
            or FileName in~ ("bootmgfw.efi", "bootmgr.efi", "bootx64.efi", "winload.efi")
        | where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("TrustedInstaller.exe", "MoUsoCoreWorker.exe", "setup.exe", "BootRec.exe", "bcdboot.exe")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName),
    (DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
        | where FileName =~ "bcdedit.exe"
        | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/set", "/copy", "/create")
        | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("bootmgr", "path", "description", "{bootmgr}", "nointegritychecks", "testsigning")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType = "BcdeditExec", FileName, FolderPath, SHA256 = "", InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine = ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName = AccountName)
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
    (ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\EFI\Microsoft\Boot\", @"\EFI\Boot\")
            or TargetFileName in~ ("bootmgfw.efi", "bootmgr.efi", "bootx64.efi", "winload.efi")
        | where ActingProcessName !has_any ("TrustedInstaller.exe", "MoUsoCoreWorker.exe", "setup.exe", "BootRec.exe", "bcdboot.exe")
        | project TimeGenerated, Host = DvcHostname, Event = "EfiFileWrite", File = TargetFileName, Path = TargetFilePath, Process = ActingProcessName, Cmd = ActingProcessCommandLine, User = ActorUsername),
    (ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
        | where ActingProcessName =~ "bcdedit.exe" or TargetProcessName =~ "bcdedit.exe"
        | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("/set", "/copy", "/create")
        | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("bootmgr", "path", "description", "{bootmgr}", "nointegritychecks", "testsigning")
        | project TimeGenerated, Host = DvcHostname, Event = "BcdeditExec", File = ActingProcessName, Path = "", Process = ParentProcessName, Cmd = ActingProcessCommandLine, User = ActorUsername)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: EFI Boot Manager Tampering (Possible CVE-2023-24932 BlackLotus / SprySOCKS UEFI Chain)
id: 4a8b6c12-7e9d-43f5-bf21-9c8a7d3e4f01
description: Write to the EFI System Partition boot manager binaries by a process other than the legitimate Windows update / setup chain. Consistent with BlackLotus-style UEFI bootkit install possibly chained with SprySOCKS.
references:
    - https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/fishmongers-arsenal-upgraded-sprysocks-windows/
    - https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2023-24932
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/17
tags:
    - attack.persistence
    - attack.defense_evasion
    - attack.t1542.003
logsource:
    category: file_event
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\EFI\Microsoft\Boot\'
            - '\EFI\Boot\'
    selection_name:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\bootmgfw.efi'
            - '\bootmgr.efi'
            - '\bootx64.efi'
            - '\winload.efi'
    filter_legit:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\TrustedInstaller.exe'
            - '\MoUsoCoreWorker.exe'
            - '\setup.exe'
            - '\BootRec.exe'
            - '\bcdboot.exe'
    condition: (selection_path or selection_name) and not filter_legit
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 (@TargetFilename:(*\\EFI\\Microsoft\\Boot\\* OR *\\efi\\microsoft\\boot\\* OR *\\EFI\\Boot\\*) OR @TargetFilename:(*\\bootmgfw.efi OR *\\bootmgr.efi OR *\\bootx64.efi OR *\\winload.efi)) -@Image:(*\\TrustedInstaller.exe OR *\\MoUsoCoreWorker.exe OR *\\setup.exe OR *\\BootRec.exe OR *\\bcdboot.exe)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| regex("(?i)\\\\(EFI\\\\Microsoft\\\\Boot\\\\|EFI\\\\Boot\\\\|bootmgfw\\.efi|bootmgr\\.efi|bootx64\\.efi|winload\\.efi)", field=TargetFileName)
| NOT regex("(?i)\\\\(TrustedInstaller|MoUsoCoreWorker|setup|BootRec|bcdboot)\\.exe", field=ContextImageFileName)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, TargetFileName, ContextImageFileName], function=count())

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High

ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2023-24932")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2023-24932")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
